key_finding: No PGM activity detected for Gpm3 even under forced overexpression; gpm3 and gpm2 gpm3 deletions show no growth defect
context: S. cerevisiae, enzyme assay in cell extracts + deletion genetics
confidence_limitations: High for the negative activity call. Limits: a single assay condition optimised for the Gpm1 reaction; absence of activity in extract does not exclude activity on another substrate or requiring a partner/modification

key_finding: 2.8 A structure of S. cerevisiae Gpm1 with bound 3-phosphoglycerate (PDB 1QHF); used here to define the active site by 4.5 A ligand contact rather than by assertion
context: S. cerevisiae Gpm1 crystal structure, tetramer, 3-PGA in chains A and B
confidence_limitations: High. Defines the reference residue set used throughout this report

claim_tested: Gpm1 active-site architecture and cofactor pocket
key_finding: 2.3 A Gpm1 structure; provides the apo/ligand reference for the catalytic His pair and arginine cluster

claim_tested: The substrate- and cofactor-binding residues are lost in Gpm3
key_finding: R14, S62, E93 assigned to catalysis and R94, R120, R121 to substrate binding in S. pombe PGM. All 6 map onto retained residues in Gpm3 (Arg13, Ser66, Glu120, Arg121, Arg147, Arg148) and in Gpm2
context: S. pombe PGM, site-directed mutagenesis with kinetics, CD, fluorescence, stability, ITC
confidence_limitations: High for residue assignment. Limit: assignments are from S. pombe, mapped to S. cerevisiae paralogs by global alignment

claim_tested: The second catalytic histidine is functionally relevant and lost in Gpm3
key_finding: Gpm1 His181Ala loses 1.6x10^4 in catalytic efficiency and shows 11-fold higher Km for 2,3-BPG. Gpm3 retains this residue as His235
confidence_limitations: High. Confirms the seed hypothesis is right that both catalytic His are present

claim_tested: The divergent C-terminal tail explains loss of mutase activity
key_finding: Removing the C-terminal 7 residues of Gpm1 abolishes mutase activity while leaving phosphatase activity unchanged. Replacing the two terminal lysines with glycines has only limited kinetic effect
context: S. cerevisiae Gpm1, truncation and substitution mutants
confidence_limitations: Moderate for Gpm3. The Gpm3 tail is present at full length and only its sequence differs (Q-G-K to E-G-F), which is a weaker perturbation than truncation

claim_tested: A dPGM-fold protein with intact catalytic His must be a mutase
key_finding: E. coli PhoE has the dPGM fold and catalytic residues but acts as a broad-specificity phosphatase, not a mutase
confidence_limitations: High as precedent. Direct relevance to Gpm3 is inference, not measurement

claim_tested: Thr20->Cys in Gpm3 is an inactivating substitution
key_finding: This position is conserved as Thr/Ser/Cys across phosphoglycerate mutases; active human BPGM carries Cys. The substitution cannot be cited as inactivating
confidence_limitations: High. Removes one of the candidate explanations

claim_tested: Gpm3 lost cofactor and substrate binding residues
key_finding: 14/20 structurally defined Gpm1 active-site positions retained in Gpm3: 4/5 catalytic, 5/7 cofactor, 5/8 substrate. Arg7, Arg59, Arg113, Arg114, Lys97, Glu86, His8, His181, Tyr89 all retained. Only 3 of the 6 substitutions sit at positions invariant among GpmA, PGAM1 and BPGM
context: Needleman-Wunsch global alignment, BLOSUM62, affine gaps; active site defined by 4.5 A contact to 3-PGA in 1QHF
confidence_limitations: High for the alignment at the core; the 56 residues of insertion make a small number of position assignments alignment-dependent

claim_tested: Gpm3 cannot form a competent substrate pocket
key_finding: phenix.superpose_pdbs of AF-Q12326-F1 v6 onto 1QHF gives 1.038 A backbone RMSD over 199 atoms. Median |difference| in side-chain distance to bound 3-PGA is 0.83 A (max 2.02 A). Catalytic His pair separation 3.15 A vs 2.79 A. Mean pLDDT 93.7 over the 20 active-site positions
context: AlphaFold DB model vs 1QHF chain B ligand
confidence_limitations: Moderate. AlphaFold builds from family templates and places canonical rotamers, so this shows the sequence is compatible with the fold, not that Gpm3 folds, is stable, or binds ligand in vivo

key_finding: All 6 substitutions are shared with S. cerevisiae Gpm2 and fixed across 5 Saccharomycetaceae Gpm3 orthologs (K. marxianus differs at 3). They are ancestral to the Gpm2/Gpm3 branch
context: Gpm3 orthologs from K. marxianus, Z. mellis, K. exigua, M. unispora, M. servazzii
confidence_limitations: Moderate. The UniRef50 members endpoint returned 0 entries, so the panel rests on 5 named orthologs plus S. cerevisiae Gpm2/Gpm3, not an exhaustive clade sample

claim_tested: Point substitutions are the only structural difference
key_finding: Gpm3 carries 56 inserted residues and zero deletions relative to Gpm1, including a 20-residue insertion between Arg59 and the Glu86 general-acid loop, and a C-terminal tail changing Q-G-K to E-G-F
context: Global alignment of Gpm1 (247 aa) and Gpm3 (303 aa)
confidence_limitations: High for the indel inventory. Whether the insertions impair function is untested; the AlphaFold model places them as ordered excursions away from the site
